issues.description: _enable_vad complects three orthogonal concerns into one boolean
issues.detail: The flag conflates 'should we emit VAD frames', 'should we listen to external VAD frames', and 'who owns endpointing'. These are separable: an emission policy, a listener policy, and an ownership identity. Decompose into named values (e.g. endpointing_owner, emit_vad_frames) so reading the code tells you what's true rather than what's familiar.

issues.description: Default change from EXTERNAL to FIXED silently rewrites time semantics for existing callers
issues.detail: TurnDetectionMode is identity-of-who-decides-end-of-turn. Flipping the default changes who owns that decision for every caller who didn't specify. That is an essential semantic change disguised as an easy default swap. Either keep EXTERNAL as default or document this as a breaking value change, not a tweak.

issues.description: Two enums (TurnDetectionMode and EndOfUtteranceMode) track the same fact in parallel places
issues.detail: FIXED was added to both, and _enable_vad inspects EndOfUtteranceMode while the public API takes TurnDetectionMode. One value (endpointing strategy) is being stored in two places, with an implicit mapping between them. Place-oriented duplication. One source of truth, derive the rest.

issues.description: split_sentences default lives in two places
issues.detail: Declared as Optional[bool]=None on InputParams, then coerced via `params.split_sentences or False` at config time. The actual default is False but the type says None is meaningful. Pick one: a real bool with default False, or honor None as 'inherit upstream'. Don't complect 'unset' with 'false'.

issues.description: Commented-out start_processing_metrics moved but not resolved
issues.detail: The dead comment was relocated from after the broadcast to before it. Either the metric call belongs there and should be uncommented, or it doesn't and should be deleted. Leaving relocated dead code is a signal that the question 'when does this turn actually start' was not answered.

issues.description: Frame-type switch is a behavior change wearing a rename's clothes
issues.detail: Switching from UserStoppedSpeakingFrame to VADUserStoppedSpeakingFrame narrows the set of triggers that finalize transcription. That's a real change in time semantics: finalization now only happens on VAD-origin stops, not on any upstream UserStoppedSpeakingFrame. Worth a test that pins which frame finalizes and which does not.

review.summary: The patch is COMPLECTED rather than SIMPLE. The core fact this code reasons about — "who owns end-of-turn detection, and therefore which frames mean what" — is spread across two enums (TurnDetectionMode, EndOfUtteranceMode), one derived boolean (_enable_vad), and a frame-type check. Adding FIXED to both enums and flipping the default is an essential semantic shift (identity of the endpointing owner) being shipped as an easy config tweak. The question that should have been asked first: what is the single value that represents "who decides the turn ended", and can every other flag be derived from it?
